headline: Old EV Batteries Find New Purpose in Energy Storage
meta_description: Companies are repurposing retired electric vehicle batteries with 70-80% capacity remaining to build megawatt-scale energy storage systems.
summary_short: A handful of companies are giving retired EV batteries a second life, converting them into large-scale energy storage through innovative engineering.
body:
A handful of companies are repurposing retired electric vehicle batteries to create megawatt-scale energy storage systems, extending the useful life of packs that still retain 70 to 80 percent of their original capacity.

Rather than discarding batteries once they lose effectiveness in vehicles, these engineers are applying clever technical solutions to transform them into stationary storage infrastructure. The approach addresses two challenges at once: it reduces electronic waste while expanding the grid's ability to store renewable energy.

This circular economy model reflects a growing recognition that an EV battery's retirement from a car doesn't mean the end of its working life. With most of their capacity intact, these packs can serve communities and power systems for years to come, making them far too valuable to waste.
quick_facts: Retired EV batteries retain 70-80% of original capacity
Multiple companies now repurpose old battery packs
New systems reach megawatt-scale energy storage levels
Clever engineering makes the conversion possible
